import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd

coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert is_takeaway to categorical variable
coffee_sales['is_takeaway'] = coffee_sales['is_takeaway'].map({0: 'In-Store', 1: 'Takeaway'})

# Create a bar chart to display the distribution of takeaway orders
takeaway_orders = coffee_sales['is_takeaway'].value_counts()
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.barplot(x=takeaway_orders.index, y=takeaway_orders.values, hue=takeaway_orders.index)
plt.title('Distribution of Takeaway Orders')
plt.xlabel('Order Type')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='Order Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd

# Convert is_takeaway to categorical variable
coffee_sales['is_takeaway'] = coffee_sales['is_takeaway'].map({0: 'In-Store', 1: 'Takeaway'})

# Create a bar chart to display the distribution of takeaway orders
takeaway_orders = coffee_sales['is_takeaway'].value_counts()

sns.barplot(x=takeaway_orders.index, y=takeaway_orders.values, hue=takeaway_orders.index)
plt.title('Distribution of Takeaway Orders')
plt.xlabel('Order Type')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='Order Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
